title: Error-correcting Mirror expert IDs
hypothesis: Redundant ECOC-style expert addresses will reduce expert misrouting under controlled bit noise, at a quantifiable serialized codebook cost compared with ordinary binary IDs.
physical_object: one shared expert decoder with 32 logical expert slots
mirror_coordinate: binary or error-correcting codeword address decoded by nearest codeword
logical_multiplicity: 32 logical experts addressable under noisy route transmission

development.allowed: select ECOC codebook generation seed using minimum distance on dev only; no fresh-dependent selection

success_gate: At flip probability .1, ECOC reduces misroute rate by >=50% relative to binary IDs, and total serialized routing payload stays <=2x binary control; no noiseless accuracy loss.
failure_gate: Redundancy cost exceeds 2x without robust accuracy gain, or learned/nearest decoding fails to correct injected noise.
boundaries: Synthetic address channel only; no real MoE router or task quality claim.
Codebook bits and decoder metadata are fully charged.
Robustness under injected bit flips is not expert capacity.

amendment_A1.reason: Initial run omitted the preregistered 3x repeated-ID control, so robustness frontier against the strongest simple redundancy control was incomplete. Initial fresh artifacts retained as exploratory.
amendment_A1.change: Add explicit 15-bit 3x repetition code control; no gates/hyperparameters changed.
